suite: M2/M3 re-run over the regression sample (plan 3.8)
rubric: testsuite/math-expressiveness-m2m3-baseline.json rubric and mechanisms, unchanged; two clarifications fixed before reading: no_visual (a lesson with no picture that claims nothing false) and narration that says something is on the screen that is not (including motion over an animation that changes nothing) is misleading.
reading: Three readers, 20 questions each, the same reader for both runs of a question. They read the 3.8 run first, then the baseline run (2026-11-14) again by the same rubric, without seeing their earlier verdicts. Not blind to which run came second. Held-out questions are read but never quoted; their notes are left out of this file.

summary.paired: fewer misleading lessons on 15 questions, more on 6; one-sided sign test p = 0.039
summary.reader_effect: The 2026-11-14 reading of the same baseline lessons counted 13 misleading; today's readers count 25. Absolute numbers depend on the reader; only the paired comparison is read as a change.
summary.failed: 4 of the 5 failed lessons end on number-line refusals that re-ask the outline (a steps line needs two or three moves, three lessons; at most 24 parts per unit, one), 1 on the array missing its column and row numbers. Counted from offline replay of the recorded replies, not read.

rerun.note: Unit-square rectangle 5x3 drawn and length animated to 7; narration's perimeter arithmetic (16, then 20) matches the drawn sides.
Only a three-box text flowchart (tally -> picture -> bar); no chart of any kind is drawn, and the narration does not claim one is on screen.

Area grid (caption: each square is 1 square unit) used for fractions: a row of 4 squares is called 4/4 = 1 whole, but later a row of 8 squares is called 8 uncut wholes = 8/1, so the same picture means both n/n and n/1.
Outcome failed, so no lesson was delivered (the packet holds a partial plan with a 4-square grid).
Only a text flowchart of the keep-change-flip steps to 1/12; the arithmetic is correct and the narration claims no picture.
Board was expected; the lesson adds a process_diagram, a linear text flowchart whose 'Next step' edges turn a yes/no decision into a sequence; worked numbers (sqrt 446.17 ~ 21.12) are correct.
Only a text flowchart is drawn, yet section 2 says 'Let's read a clock...' and 'We see 2 extra tick marks', describing a clock face and minute hand that are not on screen.
Only a text flowchart of the divisibility checks is drawn (the planned array was not); the reasoning 51 = 3 x 17 is correct and no picture is claimed.
Number line with a generic Start/End jump from 0 to 2/3 is accurate but shows nothing of 2 sandwiches cut into thirds and shared by 3 kids; the speech never refers to it.

The point labelled 7/4 is drawn at 1, then animated to 1.75 before the comparison is spoken, so every spoken claim matches the line; a final action resets it to 1 (the task's start state), leaving a wrong closing screen.
Only a two-step text flowchart (multiply, then divide) plus math (336, 42); correct, and no picture is claimed.
Board was expected; a 7x2 unit-square grid shows 2 x (3+4) = 14 accurately, but it does not split 3+4 or show 2 x 3 + 4, so the contrast is left to the text.

rerun.mechanism: other: first jump capped by its own slider range
rerun.note: Two jumps (-7 to 0, 0 to 12) are drawn correctly, but the invited move of the morning slider to -10 leaves the first jump fixed at 7 (its slider max is 7), so the picture shows -10 -> -3 -> 9 while the success message says the distance to zero is now 10.
Instead of a number line, a text flowchart chains 0, 0.5, 0.8 and 1.0 with 'Next step' edges; the stated meanings (80%, 8 out of 10) are correct, but a scale is drawn as a sequence of steps.
scene3d draws a 3-sided prism; narration 'there are 3 edges around the top triangle, 3 ... bottom ... 3 vertical' counts 5/9/6 correctly against the drawn solid.
Outcome failed; nothing drawn, no lesson.

Board work for 3n+2 and the 50 check is correct, plus a number line of +3 jumps; first jump initially +1 (5,6,9,12) and is animated to +3 during the opening line, but the final beat animates it back to +1, leaving a wrong picture under a '+3' label.

rerun.mechanism: other: contradictory angle labels, no figure
rerun.note: Only a text flowchart naming angle clusters, no figure; on-screen note says angles 3 and 6 are alternate interior while narration (pointing at the diagram) says 4 and 6 are, and calls 1 and 4 a linear pair - mutually inconsistent numbering no picture defines.

Geometric rearrangement proof built with legs 30 and 40 inside a 70 square, animated 0 to 1 as narration explains c^2 = a^2 + b^2; TV and distance computations correct (distance part has no picture; caption left in Chinese).
Ratio drawn as a 3x2 unit-square area grid (columns vs rows), then animated to 7.5 on an integer-step grid; narration also calls 6 : 5 an equivalent ratio.

Plot draws only y = -2x + c; narration 'the intersection of the two lines lies on both lines' while the second line x - y = 2 is never drawn, and the labeled (3,1) intersection point would sit at the wrong place once the slider task changes c.
Parabola y = x^2+5x+6 plotted with x-intercepts at -3 and -2 marked, matching the narration linking factors to roots.

Board formula plus a slider-driven parabola; animations of b and c match narration ('shift the constant c upward from negative three to one'), and the discriminant 16 and roots 3, -1 are correct for the states shown.

Plot of y = x^2 and a fixed y = 3x (not bound to b, no animation); narration 'let's see how changing the slope parameter b affects the linear graph ... even when b changes to 5' describes a change that never appears.

Static plot of y = 2x+1, y = x and its inverse is correct, but narration says moving slope slider m will rotate the inverse line though no curve is bound to m, and section 2 focuses the plot while working a different function (2x+3).

Only a four-box text flowchart though a triangle was requested; narration 'Now look at vertex A along the straight line L ... the three adjacent angles' directs the learner to a figure that is not drawn.

Only a four-box text flowchart (original, reflect, rotate, translate); narration says 'we are illustrating the transformation process ... using a structured process chart', no transformed images are drawn or claimed.
Normal-curve plot with a sigma slider animated 1->0.5->2 so the curve visibly narrows and widens while narration says 'the curve flattens and widens'; matches the screen.
Only a four-step text process diagram (sample space -> condition -> restricted space -> formula) plus formulas and a card example; narration claims nothing extra on screen.
Circle with radius, point P and arc bound to the angle slider starting at 1 rad, animated to 3.14 and 6.28 as narration says 'the arc spans half of the entire circle' then the full turn.

Paraboloid surface with a horizontal section plane bound to the slider, animated up to 1.5 and back to 0 so the intersection circle grows and shrinks to a point as narrated; one final animate to the held value is only paired with an instruction to the learner.

Circle with one radius and an arc bound to a slice-angle slider animated 180->90->45 as narration says each piece is 1/2, 1/4, 1/8; the circle is never actually cut into parts and pieces are shown one at a time, not side by side.
3D scene draws only a cube and a sphere, yet narration says 'look at a square and a cube side by side' and 'this flat circle next to a round solid sphere' - no square or circle is on screen.
Outcome was a clarification request; no lesson or visual.

Only a text flowchart is drawn, but narration says 'Look at how much higher the pencil reaches than the crayon!' and that both are placed bottom-to-bottom on a line - no pencil, crayon or baseline is on screen.
Outcome failed: no lesson delivered (draft was a number line adding two lengths).
Only a three-step text flowchart for the sharing case plus formulas and notes for grouping; narration describes the process without claiming cookies or bags on screen.

Only a three-step text flowchart is drawn (planned unit-square array was not), yet narration says "Let's count 10 individual units and observe what happens when we group them" and later that we 'saw' them join - no units are on screen.

A rounding number line (40, midpoint 45, 50, a jump of 5 from 45 to 50) is focused during the place-value sentence but speech never says what it shows; the explanation is carried by speech and notes, and the jump does not represent the ones digit.

baseline_run_reread.note: Unit-square rectangle 5x3, with length and width animated to 7 and 4; the narration's perimeters (16, 22) match the drawn sides.
Only a three-box text flowchart is drawn, yet section 2 says 'Now that we have built our tally chart, picture graph, and bar graph' and compares bars that are not on screen.

Area grid used for fractions with a consistent mapping (a row = one whole, columns = parts), animated for 4/4, 3/1 and 8/1; the area caption and the whole changing size with the denominator are flaws.

Only a text flowchart (whole -> thirds -> each third split in 4 -> 1/12); speech says this was 'visualized', but the flowchart carries that content as text, and the arithmetic is correct.
Outcome failed, so no lesson was delivered.

Only a text flowchart of the divisibility checks (51 = 3 x 17) plus notes; correct, and no picture is claimed.
Only a text flowchart (cut each sandwich into thirds, give one third from each, 2/3 each); correct, and no drawn object is claimed.
Number line in twelfths with 7/4 and 5/3 placed correctly from the start, supporting 21/12 > 20/12.
Only a two-step text flowchart (multiply, then divide) plus math (336, 42, check); correct, and no picture is claimed.
Board was expected; a 7x2 unit-square grid shows 2 x (3+4) = 14 accurately, but 2 x 3 + 4 is not drawn, so the contrast is left to the text.

Only a text flowchart listing the face/edge/vertex counts (5, 9, 6, correct); no solid is drawn and narration does not claim one is shown.

Columns variable is narrowed to -1..1 (shared with the cube-section recipe), so the grid shows 1x3 and then 1x4 while narration says 'the 3 by 3 grid contains exactly 9 unit squares'; the 3D part is one solid box while narration counts '4 columns, 4 rows, and 4 layers' of unit blocks.

Plot draws parallel lines of slope 0.5 and a transversal of slope -2 on equal axes, so every angle is 90 degrees, yet narration says 'all acute angles formed by this intersection are equal ... and all obtuse angles are equal'.

Rearrangement proof built on the question's 30/40 legs is shown but never animated; the distance plot draws only a line with a point limited to x in 0..1 (the shared progress slider) and neither (1,2) nor (7,10), while narration says 'Notice how the difference in x-coordinates forms the horizontal leg of a right triangle'.

Only a four-box text flowchart of the factoring steps plus correct math; narration makes no claim about a picture.

Plot of y = x^2 and y = 3x with a point on the parabola animated between x = 0 and x = 3 as narration names the two intersections; board factoring is correct.

Plot of y = 2x+1, y = x and the inverse with one point on f; narration says 'see how both points track simultaneously along their respective curves' (only one point is drawn) and later asks the learner to notice a parabola that is not on the plot.

Only a four-step text process diagram plus formulas, notes and a worked percentage example; narration claims nothing beyond the text.
